title: Make the signal costly enough to mean something.
dek: In Chapter 3 of Rory Sutherland's Alchemy, signalling explains why choices that look inefficient can communicate trust, status, commitment, and quality.

marginNote.label: Apprenticeship Note
marginNote.body: A signal works when it carries a meaningful cost or constraint. Before removing an apparently inefficient feature, ask what confidence, identity, or trust it is helping the other person perceive.

canon.heading: Let the signal carry information the claim cannot.
canon.standfirst: Read Chapter 3, "Signalling," from Rory Sutherland's Alchemy on PDF pages 134-168. Study how costly, visible, or seemingly irrational choices can communicate qualities that are otherwise difficult to verify, then stop at PDF page 168.
canon.readerIntro: Read this chapter as a study of hidden information. Mark the cases where a cost, constraint, ritual, or visible choice makes trust or quality legible, and distinguish a meaningful signal from empty theatre. Then audit one product, service, or brand: name the quality it wants to communicate, the evidence currently available, and one signal whose cost would make the promise more credible. Stop at PDF page 168.

blocks.label: 01 / Look for the hidden quality
paragraphs: Signalling becomes useful when one party knows something another party cannot easily verify. Start by naming the hidden quality: competence, commitment, taste, reliability, or status.
Notice where a conventional efficiency lens misses the information carried by a visible choice.

blocks.label: 02 / Study why cost can create credibility
paragraphs: A signal is more credible when it would be difficult for a low-quality or uncommitted actor to imitate. The cost may be money, time, effort, risk, constraint, or foregone convenience.
Separate a cost that screens for commitment from a cost that merely adds friction.

blocks.label: 03 / Distinguish signal from decoration
paragraphs: Not every conspicuous feature communicates something useful. Ask whether the audience can connect the signal to a quality that matters and whether the connection survives scrutiny.
Look for the point at which a meaningful signal turns into performance detached from the underlying promise.

blocks.label: 04 / Audit one promise
paragraphs: Choose one offer whose important quality is hard for a customer to judge before purchase. Write the hidden quality, the current proof, and the easiest way a weak provider could imitate it.
Then propose one costly or constraining signal and explain why it would be difficult to fake without delivering the quality itself.

closeReading: What hidden quality is each signalling example trying to make visible?
Why does a costly or constraining signal communicate more reliably than a simple claim?
Which apparently irrational behaviour becomes intelligible once signalling enters the explanation?
How can you distinguish a signal that helps a customer judge quality from decorative theatre?
Choose one offer: what signal could make its promise more credible, and what would make that signal difficult to fake?

principle.heading: Make the promise legible through commitment.
principle.body: When quality or intent is hard to observe directly, a visible cost, constraint, or ritual can carry information that a claim cannot. Design signals that are difficult to fake and connected to the quality they promise.
principle.example: A specialist consultancy publishes a narrow client-fit policy, declines work outside its method, and shares a demanding diagnostic before proposing a project. The constraints signal focus and competence because a weak generalist would be less willing to bear them.
principle.practice: Choose one offer. Write the hidden quality, the current claim, the easiest imitation, and one costly signal. State why the signal would be difficult to fake without actually delivering the promised quality.

output.heading: Let the proof do more than the promise.
output.body: Find the quality people cannot easily verify, then design a visible commitment whose cost makes that quality easier to believe.

signals.heading: Four current signals on making commitment visible, costly, and easier to trust.

fieldNotes.title: OpenAI acquires Pierre to make agentic code review more legible
fieldNotes.whatHappened: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company, whose open-source developer tools include Trees, Diffs, Highlights, and Code Storage. OpenAI said Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source and that its tools will help Codex connect code shipped with the decisions people make.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: Reviewable work is a signal of trustworthy work: the diff, history, and edit path let another person inspect what an agent did instead of accepting a polished claim. The credibility comes from preserving the costly trail of decisions, not from saying the agent is reliable.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether Codex makes review evidence faster and more complete as agent output scales, and whether open-source continuity preserves trust in the acquisition.

fieldNotes.title: Meta buys Conductor as agentic teams become a product category
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Meta acquired Conductor, a startup that lets developers deploy multiple agents into parallel workspaces. TechCrunch reported that Conductor's core features will continue for now, but its cloud service will shut down on Nov. 20 and cloud data will then be deleted.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The acquisition is a commitment signal about where Meta wants its next interface to be, but the shutdown creates a second signal for customers: continuity is only credible when data and workflows have a safe path through the transition. A bold future promise cannot erase a concrete switching cost.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether Meta gives Conductor users a credible migration and retention path before the shutdown, and whether the acquired product becomes a coherent experience rather than another capability announcement.

fieldNotes.title: Levi's spends four hours per second to make craft the proof
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Levi's holiday campaign, “Let's Get Fuzzy,” uses a 60-second stop-motion claymation film inspired by its 1995 Clayman ad. Marketing Dive reported that each second required four hours of filming, with the set and characters made by hand and no AI used in filming.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The labor is not just production trivia; it is evidence for the brand's claim about craft and human creativity. In a feed full of fast synthetic output, visible effort can make a familiar promise harder to imitate and therefore more believable.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the handcrafted signal transfers from film enjoyment to sweater consideration, and whether the brand can sustain the craft association beyond a single expensive holiday execution.

fieldNotes.title: Disney makes social commerce a bounded holiday event
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Disney's first TikTok Shop Super Brand Day runs Nov. 4-10 with more than 20 participating brands, creator storytelling, paid media, and limited TikTok Shop exclusives including a Loungefly holiday mini backpack.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The campaign makes commitment visible through a bounded window, a curated cast, and products that cannot be bought in the same way forever. The shopping experience becomes a story with a time-bound consequence rather than an endless shelf.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the event creates completed purchases and repeat discovery, or only a short-lived spike that leaves the broader brand relationship unchanged.

tweets.author: signüll
tweets.title: Credibility, distribution, and mystique as visible signals
tweets.summary: This fragment describes a sequence in which joining a lab supplies credibility, frequent posting converts credibility into distribution, and leaving creates mystique. It is a compact example of how visible commitments and constraints can carry meaning beyond a direct claim.
tweets.text:
the best way to build an x following is to join a lab, tweet a lot, & then leave.

joining obviously gives you credibility. tweeting a bunch converts that credibility into distribution. then leaving converts that distribution into mystique for your next thing.

signals.tweetHeading: One fragment on how visible commitments become signals.
